questions.question: A patient presents with a lesion affecting the greater petrosal nerve. Which of the following ganglia contains the cell bodies of the postganglionic parasympathetic neurons that receive innervation from this nerve?

During a surgical dissection of the popliteal fossa, the surgeon identifies neurovascular structures. From posterior to anterior (superficial to deep), what is the correct relative arrangement of these main structures?
options: Popliteal artery, popliteal vein, tibial nerve
Tibial nerve, popliteal vein, popliteal artery
Popliteal vein, tibial nerve, popliteal artery
Tibial nerve, popliteal artery, popliteal vein

questions.question: A surgeon is mobilizing the first part of the subclavian artery medial to the anterior scalene muscle. Which of the following arteries typically arises directly from this first section of the subclavian artery?
The thoracic duct ascends through the posterior mediastinum before draining lymph back into the venous circulation. At which specific anatomical site does the thoracic duct typically terminate?
options: Azygos vein at the level of the T4 vertebra
Superior vena cava near the right atrium
Left venous angle (junction of left internal jugular and left subclavian veins)

questions.question: An severe case of otitis media in the tympanic cavity erodes through its thin roof (the tegmen tympani). Infection spreading superiorly through this structure will directly enter which cranial compartment?
